faq.q: What is the origin of Saleem?
faq.a: Saleem is associated with Arabic. Saleem is Arabic سَلِيم (Salīm), meaning 'sound, free from defect'.
Yes — the underlying form سَلِيم is Arabic.
Saleem can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Saleem should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س ل م is Quranic, but Salīm is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Saleem mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Saleem is rendered سلیم and carries the sense سلیم، تندرست.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Saleem, saleem. Script forms are سلیم, سَلِيم, सलीम.

faq.q: Is Saleem a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
